result.title: PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents
result.summary: Terminal rewards make multi-turn agents trainable without step-level annotations, but group-relative advantages provide little guidance about which intermediate decisions to adjust. Failed trajectories also contain reasonable actions, while unfavorable decision patterns can recur as training proceeds. We introduce PEARL (Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning), which improves local credit assignment without an additional critic. Given two continuations from the same history with different outcomes, PEARL locates their first divergence and builds a feature representation of each branch's local decision. It clusters these decision features in recent failure and success memories to identify recurring local patterns. Using this pattern memory, PEARL selectively strengthens negative advantages at lower-reward decisions, while leaving positive advantages and the base policy optimizer unchanged. On AppWorld, PEARL improves over ARPO on Normal and Challenge tasks at both 4B and 8B scales. On ALFWorld, it achieves 97.9% mean success at 4B, 2.7 points above the strongest baseline, while remaining competitive at 8B. Ablations of shaping location, success-bank filtering, and memory window support the value of selective, recurring-pattern-based updates.

AI.brief_summary: PEARL 提出无需额外 critic 的多轮 agent 强化学习框架：对同一历史的两条不同结局轨迹定位首次分歧，构建局部分支的决策特征并在成功/失败记忆库中聚类，识别反复出现的局部决策模式，从而有选择地强化低回报决策的负优势，在 AppWorld、ALFWorld 上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属纯文本多轮 agent 的训练期信用分配，未涉及视觉或多模态内部状态；其「首次分歧定位＋模式记忆聚类」的局部贡献分配机制，可能为 LVR 轨迹训练中的中间步骤监督与贡献分配提供可核查线索。
